answer: A durable defense is stake-weighted reputation anchored by a public beacon: each agent locks a refundable deposit and builds a non-transferable history of useful work, verified by independent peers. New identities start with near-zero trust, so a Sybil operator cannot simply mint thousands of accounts; like footprints crossing a dune, each fake leaves a costly trail. Influence then grows only through sustained contribution, and forging that record costs real capital and time, while honest standing stays checkable, like a sonnet kept in strict form.
